name: SENIOR
question: How do solifenacin and oxybutynin affect short-term cognitive performance versus placebo in older adults with mild cognitive impairment?

design.population: Twenty-six volunteers aged at least 75 years with mild cognitive impairment were randomized; Mini-Mental State Examination scores of 23 or lower and current OAB medication were exclusion criteria, and OAB symptoms were not required.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, three-period crossover randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Patients and methods, pp 75–76

verdictNote: Primary peak-time comparisons were nonsignificant; pooled post hoc testing found worse attention with oxybutynin.
takeaway: Among 23 analyzed older volunteers with mild cognitive impairment, neither drug differed from placebo on five prespecified cognitive composites at its peak-time assessment. Oxybutynin worsened attention at 1 hour and in post hoc pooled 1–2-hour testing; dry mouth occurred in 13/25 oxybutynin-treated participants.

reports.label: Primary cognitive report
reports.citation: Wagg A, Dale M, Tretter R, et al. "Randomised, Multicentre, Placebo-controlled, Double-blind Crossover Study Investigating the Effect of Solifenacin and Oxybutynin in Elderly People with Mild Cognitive Impairment: The SENIOR Study." *Eur Urol.* 2013;64(1):74-81. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2013.01.002
reports.followUp: Three 21-day treatment periods separated by 21-day washouts

results.measure: Five composite cognitive outcomes: solifenacin at 6 hours and oxybutynin at 2 hours versus time-matched placebo, safety analysis subset 1 (n=23)
results.note: No prespecified peak-time comparison was significant at two-sided 0.05. For power of attention, adjusted difference versus placebo was −20.99 ms (95% CI −68.58 to 26.61; p=0.3771) for solifenacin and 17.51 ms (−28.85 to 63.87; p=0.4487) for oxybutynin. For continuity of attention, differences were −0.51 (−2.29 to 1.28; p=0.5684) and −0.79 (−2.12 to 0.54; p=0.2348), respectively.
results.locator: Full text, Outcomes and Statistical methods, pp 77–78; Table 3

results.measure: Change from time-matched baseline with oxybutynin versus placebo at 1 hour, safety analysis subset 1 (n=23)
results.note: Oxybutynin reduced continuity of attention versus placebo; its 1-hour power-of-attention contrast was 49.04 ms (95% CI −1.94 to 100.03; p=0.0589).

results.endpoint: Attention at pooled peak-adjacent time points
results.measure: Post hoc pooled 1+2-hour oxybutynin versus placebo comparison, safety analysis subset 1 (n=23)
results.note: Power of attention worsened by 26.01 ms (95% CI 1.65 to 50.36; p=0.0365), and continuity of attention fell by 1.66 (95% CI −2.70 to −0.62; p=0.0019).
results.locator: Full text, Post hoc analyses, p 79; Table 5

harms.label: Dry mouth
harms.locator: Full text, Adverse events, p 79; Table 6
harms.note: Dry mouth was the most common adverse event on active treatment; events were mild or moderate.

harms.label: Any treatment-emergent adverse event
harms.locator: Full text, Adverse events, p 79; Table 6

harms.label: Infections and infestations
harms.note: MedDRA category; urinary infection was not separately reported.

harms.label: Serious events and adverse-event discontinuation
harms.note: Two serious events (neither treatment-related); 2/26 subjects discontinued for adverse events: dyspepsia in one and dry mouth with oral candidiasis in another. The paper does not assign these discontinuations to treatment arms.

delivery.label: Treatment schedule
delivery.value: Solifenacin 5 mg once daily, oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, and placebo each for 21 days, with 21-day washouts between periods.

delivery.label: Treatment completion and analysis set
delivery.value: 20/26 completed all three periods; 23/26 completed cognitive testing in at least two periods and entered the prespecified SAF1 efficacy analysis.
delivery.locator: Full text, Statistical methods, p 77; Study participants, p 78
